quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes causes control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and then apply it again. If you lock your rear brake on a surface with good grip while stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: What color are service signs?
questions.explanation: Service signs are blue with white letters. They show where you can find rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: If bright sunlight makes it hard to see your turn signals, what should you do?

options.text: Keep using the mechanical turn signals.
Honk your horn to warn other drivers.

questions.explanation: Use hand signals when bright sunlight makes your turn signals hard to see. It is very important to clearly tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects steering, which affects your balance.
It stops the front brake from working.
It prevents you from speeding up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects steering, which affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering difficult. This affects your ability to stay balanced. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It brakes automatically by learning your riding habits.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems. When you use the rear brake, it also uses the front brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your specific motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: In dangerous areas, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping centers, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Cover the clutch and both brake levers so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, if you crash. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: Is a helmet required for a motorcycle operator?

options.text: Not required if you have ridden for more than two years.

questions.explanation: In Virginia, motorcycle operators and passengers must wear helmets. A good helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What can cause collisions involving motorcycles?

options.text: Honking the horn at the wrong time

questions.explanation: Following too closely behind another vehicle causes many motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally move into another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before you enter a turn.

questions.question: Which of the following affects a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content depends on three main things: how much alcohol a person drinks, how fast they drink it, and their body weight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black symbols tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a divided roadway is coming.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning in a curve:

options.text: Should only be done smoothly and carefully.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done smoothly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change can make the rear wheel skid.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you properly, which means:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely reach the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be about one foot higher than your waist when standing next to the bike.
Your feet should touch the ground comfortably when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should touch the ground comfortably when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet touch the ground comfortably while you sit on the seat. Make sure a motorcycle fits before you ride it.

questions.question: When entering a turn, you should:
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before entering a turn. Fast turns can cause you to leave your lane or ride off the road.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you stay visible to other drivers and avoid hazards. It should discourage other drivers from entering your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything you need to see.
Turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors.
Signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before you change lanes, even if you use your mirrors.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Ride one behind the other in a single line.

questions.explanation: Staggered formation lets the group stay together while giving each rider enough space to be safe. Switch to single-file when turning, in curves, or entering or leaving the road.

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Be loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Fit snug so they don't flap in the wind.
Be tight so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snug so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap, but loose enough so you can move freely.

questions.question: Smaller vehicles appear to be ________ and slower than they really are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast or far away a small vehicle like a motorcycle is. Do not assume that drivers of bigger vehicles can correctly judge your speed and location.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:
questions.explanation: Gloves help you grip better and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made from strong material.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving as separate actions. Never brake while swerving because this can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: The gearshift is located:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.
